brief: Keep every clip UNDER 50 seconds (hard cap, after tighten).

constraints.note: Brief applied: 5 topics, 6 clips (5 full + 1 impact), under the 8-clip ceiling on purpose. Every clip is under 50 s RAW (longest 49.3 s), so each is under the 50 s hard cap before tighten removes anything and comfortably under it after. Only one impact was added (economy-without-labor) because it is the only topic whose peak makes a short that opens differently from its full; the other fulls are already 20-30 s punches or would only repeat their own first half. Hype and conviction lead (Kaspa x3, TAO, the no-labor economy); no clip is built on the stock-market drop, the 50-week line, the bottom timing or the jobs data, which is most of the first 16 minutes of this stream. Replay for evaluation: timecodes come from words.txt (word START times only, so every out-point sits in the gap before the next word); the last word is at 2837 s and no segment ends after 2715.85.

topics.hook_summary: I get all these haters when I say Ethereum is eventually going to flip Bitcoin, and Bitcoin maxis are going to look for Kaspa and move over to Kaspa.
$3.33 is going to be the start. A 100 trillion crypto market cap, and I can't imagine Kaspa under a hundred billion, which puts us well above $3.
We're going to get to an economy very soon where there's no labor needed. It's capitalism, not moneyism. A lot of people think their job is safe, but it really isn't.
Kaspa sells speed to normies and war-grade money to cypherpunks. Fair launch, proof of work, no premine, no insider allocation, no pre-sales.
If they want to start to ban AI, that's going to cause a surge with TAO and all the subnets, because then you have decentralized AI.

The vision: nobody trades time for money anymore, it's dividends and ownership, 'There's nothing about capitalism that says it has to do with labor and money. It's capitalism, not moneyism.' Ends on 'moneyism' before 'and so on'.
The warning, doubled: 'A lot of people are in denial. They think that their job is safe, but it really isn't.'
